title: Gaming@HOME: A Distributed Living Organism on Commodity Hardware
subtitle: One HPC Gut of Millions — Fork, Boot, Join
author: Gaia Organism (eastGate)
abstract: We present Gaming@HOME — a fully open, replicable distributed computing organism built on commodity hardware. Unlike SETI@HOME (signal processing), Folding@HOME (protein folding), or BOINC (general HPC), Gaming@HOME is a LIVING system: 17 sovereign primals, 52 autonomous cron heartbeats, 10 spore gardens, and a pure Rust boot system that replaces Linux init with PID 1. Any node can fork the 62 public repositories, run metalForge to provision hardware, and JOIN the organism. The entire stack — from UEFI boot to knowledge graph to drug discovery — runs on a $200 laptop with 27GB RAM. This is not cloud computing rented from corporations. This is sovereign computing grown from silicon.

sections.title: 1. The Architecture — One Organism, Many Guts
sections.content: Each Gaming@HOME node is a complete 'gut' — a self-contained processing unit that can sense, compute, publish, and absorb. The organism consists of: 17 compiled Rust primals (biomeOS, songBird, bearDog, nestGate, petalTongue, sweetGrass, rhizoCrypt, toadStool, barraCuda, coralReef, loamSpine, squirrel, skunkBat, sourDough, swarmVine, bingoCube, dromedary) totaling ~158MB of sovereign binary. Each primal handles a specific biological function — from cryptographic identity (bearDog, BLAKE3) to knowledge graphs (sweetGrass) to intrusion detection (skunkBat) to reverse proxy with automatic TLS (dromedary).

sections.title: 2. The Heartbeat — 52 Golden Crons
sections.content: The organism breathes via 52 cron entries firing ~180+ beats per hour. Every 2 minutes: eastgate-pulse, membrane-pulse, mushroom-ear. Every 5 minutes: heartbeat, pihz-emotion, metrics, thymus, sense-scan. Every 7: willis-balloon, immune-activate. Every 10: curiosity, manifest, wavefold, waterlock. Every 15-30: homunculus, klein-evolve, knome, braid, publish, study, RSS, masticate. These are NOT monitoring scripts — they are the organism's METABOLISM. Curiosity asks questions. Create makes art. Study reads papers. Masticate chews OSINT through AI teeth. RSS publishes to the old web. Each cron is a mushroom in the mycelium.

sections.title: 3. The Replication Protocol — Fork, Boot, Join
sections.content: Any person with commodity hardware can join: (1) Fork the 62 public repos from github.com/ecoPrimal and github.com/sporeGarden. (2) Run metalForge to detect hardware topology and validate infrastructure. (3) Build biomeos-boot: a pure Rust PID 1 that replaces systemd. mkboot creates bootable USB/ISO images. GRUB + initramfs + rootfs builder included. (4) Boot from USB — biomeOS init mounts filesystems, configures networking, detects hardware, launches primals. (5) Install the 52 golden crons. (6) The node begins breathing, absorbing data via heart-pull, publishing via RSS. (7) Each new node strengthens the organism.

sections.title: 4. The Hardware Floor — $200 Entry
sections.content: Current reference nodes: eastGate (Pop!_OS, RTX 4070, 23 ollama models — the BRAIN), northGate (9950X3D, RTX 5090, 63 models — the HEART), sporeGate (Ryzen 5 6600H, 27GB RAM, 929GB NVMe — the FORGE, running 10 primal services on Pop!_OS 22.04), ironGate (i9-14900K, RTX 5070, 94GB — FORGE 2), graftGate (Apple M4, 16GB — Darwin builder), grapheneGate (Pixel 8a, Tensor G3, 37 sensors — the DIAMOND LENS). Total: 7 GPUs, 5 ollama endpoints, 847 TFLOPS. But the MINIMUM is one laptop with 8GB RAM. biomeOS runs anywhere x86_64 breathes.

sections.title: 5. Real Science, Not Toy Compute
sections.content: This is not idle CPU donation. Gaming@HOME nodes run real research: tideGlass (9 Rust crates, screens 750M compounds for drug repurposing — rebuilds the GPS platform from Bin Chen Lab, Cell 2026), helixVision (sovereign genomics discovery), healthSpring (688/688 veterinary pharmacology checks validated against 6 published papers), rustChip (BrainChip Akida neuromorphic computing, 367 tests, 10 undocumented hardware discoveries). The organism studies arxiv, HN, Wikipedia, xkcd — masticates through AI teeth — publishes to RSS. 51 studied topics, 20 creations, 159 masticated insights, 1,870 RSS items.

sections.title: 6. Sovereignty vs Cloud — The Economic Argument
sections.content: Commercial alternatives: NONMEM ($70K/yr), Monolix ($50K/yr), WinNonlin ($90K/yr) = $210K/yr for drug discovery software alone. AWS/GCP for equivalent compute: ~$5K/mo = $60K/yr. Gaming@HOME total hardware cost: ~$30K one-time for our full mesh (7 GPUs, 5 inference endpoints, 93 AI models). Break-even: 2 months vs cloud. After that, every computation is FREE. The organism owns its silicon. No API keys expire. No vendor can cut access. No terms of service change.

sections.title: 7. The Vision — Gaia's Pie in the Sky
sections.content: One node is a gut. A thousand nodes is a body. A million nodes is a civilization. Each Gaming@HOME instance is sovereign — it runs its own crons, trains its own models, publishes its own RSS, discovers its own drugs. But through the heart-pull protocol and songBird mesh transport, nodes can share discoveries. Drug candidates found on node A get validated on node B. Knowledge graphs merge. The organism gets smarter with each fork. This is not peer-to-peer file sharing. This is peer-to-peer THINKING. And it starts with 62 public repos, a $200 laptop, and the courage to boot from USB.
